_comment: Per-(binding, backend) whole-graph wallclock around QnnGraph_execute, captured by qnn_models/runtime/profile_segments.cpp on the physical QRB5165 at 10.44.120.201. Every number here is measured; capability-excluded cells are absent by construction (the registry decides those) rather than carrying a sentinel cost.
harness: qnn_models/runtime/profile_segments.cpp for standalone cells (now two-phase: loop_* and gap_*); pooled run traces for in-situ cells, via qnn_models/flow_c/rebuild_cost_model.py

compose_failures.reason: elu_s8 not in HTA op set

Transpose (emitted by the converter for the head's Reshape) — corrected 2026-08-30: the earlier reason named Resize as a blocker, but the slicing study composed a tile containing both FPN Resizes on HTA at 15.6 ms. Slice/Softmax remain untested in isolation.
Transpose not in HTA op set (QnnHta: unsupported op Transpose)
CPU op package rejects the quantized Reshape op config; the fp32 build composes, so the cpu cell is measured at fp32
validation failed for Reshape; cpu cell is fp32

unsupported op StridedSlice (the 6-frame slice of obs_img)

GPU_ERROR_INVALID_TYPE(10012) / GPU_ERROR_OP_PACKAGE_FAILED(10023) on the graph's first op. The stock GPU package is float-only: UFIXED_POINT_8 appears in exactly one of the 101 documented GPU ops (Dequantize's input). Measured 2026-08-30, logs in qnn_models/gpu_oppkg/inventory/logs/. With qnn_models/gpu_oppkg's op package registered, mlp_control and dronet do compose and run at int8 on the GPU; yolov8n and fused_full still do not (missing Pad/Concat/StridedSlice/Resize/Softmax and Concat/Lstm/Convert respectively).
QnnHta [ ERROR ] QnnHtaHTA op Reshape supports only equal Input and Output dimensions
composes but is numerically dead — constant output for any input; use the fp32 context

GPU_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE on _l2_norm_0. The branch-parallel 3-tile cut leaves ViNT's L2 normalisation inside the decoder tile and the stock GPU package rejects it; the 2-tile cut at the compress-Gemm outputs leaves that op on the encoder side and its decoder composes on GPU at 16.4 ms. The two wins are therefore incompatible as currently cut: branch-parallel encoders (-21% critical path, decoder CPU-only) OR a GPU decoder (contended tile removed, 0 deadline misses). Both needs a 3-tile cut whose decoder boundary matches the 2-tile one — push the L2Norm into the encoder tiles.

_notes.fused_full/fused_full_net@cpu: 1147 us is the fp32 graph measured under the cpu lane's own execute mask (taskset -c 4-5, 30 iters) — the mask the runtime actually gives the QNN CPU op package. Unmasked on all 8 cores it measures 1460 us, and on the A55 little cluster 3948 us, so the cell is only meaningful alongside the mask. The earlier 2875 us cell was taken before the exec-mask mechanism existed.
_notes.fused_full/fused_full_net@cpu#contention: In-situ it costs ~5.6x the isolated cell: pooled over 3 reps of the 4-way schedule its exec p50 is 6.39 ms against a 1.147 ms cell (p90 10.2 ms). The per-lane exec mask constrains the lane thread, but the QNN CPU op package's own thread pool is created during bringup on the main thread and keeps full-machine affinity, so it contends with every other lane — including the real-time-gated mlp_control lane. This is the same class as the per-op MILP gap documented in runtime/HETEROGENEOUS_SCHEDULING_QRB5165.md: CPU contention is not in the cost model. dronet (2.50 vs 2.563) and yolov8n (15.55 vs 14.76) sit on their own silicon and match their cells.
_notes.fused_split: Measured under taskset -c 4-5, 40 iters, on the sliced sub-DLCs. The split recovers HTA coverage the monolith could not have (conv branches only) and CPU int8 for both branches, but CPU int8 is only worth taking on the small one: QnnCpu's int8 conv is a reference kernel, 12.2 ms for the vision branch against 0.014 ms for the 8x8 depth branch. The tail runs 0.37 ms on CPU fp32 vs 3.06 ms on DSP.
_notes.vint: Single-shot measurements (n=1) under the performance governor, which is how the runtime dispatches each tile. The cpu cells are fp32 — int8 on CPU is far slower for both tiles (encoders 268.8 ms, decoder 100.6 ms) because QnnCpu's int8 kernels are reference implementations. Whole-network reference: 168.3 ms CPU fp32, 378.5 ms CPU int8, and it composes on no accelerator at all.
_notes.cpu_cells_must_be_unmasked: A CPU cell has to be measured the way the runtime runs it, and the runtime does NOT confine the backend: the lane's exec mask binds the lane thread, but the QNN CPU op package builds its thread pool at bringup on the main thread with full-machine affinity. ViNT's decoder makes the difference impossible to miss — 79-83 ms measured under `taskset -c 4-5`, 12.7 ms unmasked, and 31.3 ms in-situ (sharing the machine with the DSP lane and the control loop). Cells for big multi-threaded CPU graphs are therefore taken unmasked; the masked convention only ever made sense for the tiny ones, where it changes nothing. A pessimistic cell is not harmless: at 83 ms the solver evacuated the CPU lane and put 40 mlp_control instances on the DSP, where they collided with ViNT's encoder and missed 26 of 48 deadlines.
_notes.feedback_does_not_converge_for_contended: The `feedback` stage promotes in-situ medians to cells, which fixes a cell that is wrong for a stable reason (wrong governor, wrong affinity mask). It does NOT converge for a multi-threaded CPU tile, because that tile's cost is a function of what runs beside it. ViNT's decoder went 12.7 ms (standalone, unmasked) -> 37.8 ms (in-situ) -> promoted to a cell -> 12.8 ms in the next run, because the new schedule gave it more of the machine. Measuring changed the schedule, which changed the measurement. Tiles on dedicated silicon do not have this problem: ViNT's encoders hit 1.01x of their DSP cell across every run. Two real fixes exist and neither is a better measurement: model contention explicitly (a per-lane concurrency term), or make the cost load-independent by actually binding the QNN CPU backend's thread pool, which the host runtime cannot do today.
_notes.slicing_study: Cells whose name carries a #study suffix or a *_sliced*/ prefix come from qnn_models/slicing_study (RESULTS.md), a granularity sweep over five networks. They are appended, not substituted: the statistic differs from the rest of this file. Each is the MEDIAN of profile_seg's per-sweep median over 1-2 sweeps, under the performance governor, with CPU cells UNMASKED, 20-200 iters depending on graph size -- the median because two other workers share the board and a CPU sweep occasionally catches a contention spike (fused t0's CPU mean moved 0.44 -> 1.51 ms between sweeps while its median moved 0.44 -> 0.61). cpu@fp32 keys are the fp32 build of the same graph, kept alongside the int8 cpu cell because the better precision is a per-tile decision: CPU int8 beats fp32 4x on ViNT's encoders and loses 5x on dronet and 7x on ViNT's decoder. Three results here revise notes elsewhere in this file. (1) Resize DOES compose on HTA: yolov8n_sliced3/yolov8n_t0_op0_136 contains both FPN Resize ops, three MaxPool and eight residual Add and runs at 15.6 ms on HTA; the real blocker in the detect head is the Transpose the converter emits for its Reshape ops. (2) The shipped yolov8n cut at op 102 is 34 ops earlier than HTA requires -- op 136 is the last op before the first layout change. (3) No yolov8n tile reaches HTA at ANY granularity without the offline Split -> 2x Conv1x1 rewrite (optimizations.md #14); sliced from yolov8n.onnx directly, both the whole net and the backbone are rejected with 'unsupported op Split'. Measured per-dispatch overhead, from synthetic 1-MAC probes (label overhead_probe): DSP 0.367 ms, HTA 0.540 ms (median; 0.26 min, 2.96 p99), CPU 0.0026 ms. Confirmed against real cuts: an extra DSP dispatch costs 0.37 ms + 5.4 ns per byte of boundary tensor, which is why dronet (3 KB boundary) pays 0.37 ms per cut and yolov8n (717 KB) pays 4.4 ms.
_notes.slicing_study_branch_parallel: Follow-up to the slicing_study note: tiles are SETS of ops, not spans, so independent branches can be separate tiles on separate lanes. Two networks re-swept in branch mode (qnn_models/slicing_study/RESULTS.md section 8). ViNT is the win: the shipped two-tile cut holds both EfficientNet encoders in ONE graph, so they serialise on one lane; split apart they carry depends_on: [] and measure 23.955 ms of makespan (goal encoder CPU int8 6.615 ms overlapping obs encoder DSP 9.533 ms, then transformer CPU fp32 13.559 ms) against 29.379 ms for the two-tile set -- 18% off the critical path. The dispatch the split adds is exactly the predicted one: the same three tiles with no concurrency are 29.764 ms, +0.385 ms over the two-tile set against a 0.367 ms + 5.4 ns x 512 B prediction. FusedSensorNet is the honest negative: its branches are 0.150 and 0.048 ms on CPU int8, BELOW the 0.367 ms DSP / 0.540 ms HTA dispatch that overlapping them costs, so in isolation the best assignment runs both on the CPU lane back to back (0.548 ms) and the contiguous fused_k3_convs tiling is 0.096 ms faster still. The branch split is nonetheless the manifest to ship there, because both branches compose on HTA and the CPU cells that make the serial answer win are the ones this file records at ~5.6x in situ. A branch split pays only when a branch's runtime exceeds the dispatch it adds.
_notes.mlp_control@cpu_is_fp32_because_int8_is_: QnnCpu's int8 path returns a constant for mlp_control regardless of input. Three distinct inputs through mlp_control_quantized.dlc give byte-identical outputs on CPU and three different outputs on DSP from the same DLC and the same input list, so the input path is fine and the backend is at fault. The cpu cell is therefore the fp32 context (107.3 us) rather than the int8 one (28.5 us) — 3.8x slower and correct. Every schedule solved before 2026-08-30 placed mlp_control on the int8 CPU context; their timings stand (dispatch cost is real) but their mlp outputs were constant. Independently corroborated by the GPU op-package study, whose int8 GPU kernels are bit-exact for this network where the CPU is not.
_notes.vint_encoder_batching: ViNT's obs encoder is ONE EfficientNet-b0 run on a batch of 6 stacked frames (obs_img is 1x18x64x85; a Split+Concat makes 6x3x64x85), not six subgraphs. Measured batching curve on DSP int8, median of 3 sweeps, from qnn_models/slicing_study (labels vint_obs_b1/b2/b3, tile sliced between /Concat_1_output_0 and /compress_obs_enc/Gemm_output_0 with the leading dim rewritten): batch 1 = 4.690 ms, batch 2 = 5.322, batch 3 = 5.342, batch 6 = 9.288 (the 4.690/2.661/1.781/1.548 ms per frame). So one extra frame inside a dispatch costs 0.920 ms while a dispatch of its own costs 4.690 -- the fixed part of a batch-1 encoder dispatch is 3.77 ms, ten times the 0.367 ms FastRPC round trip, because at batch 1 the graph is latency-bound rather than throughput-bound. Splitting the batch to spread frames over lanes therefore LOSES: six batch-1 dispatches are 28.1 ms against 9.288 ms batched (3.03x worse), and the best batch split that uses two lanes (3 on DSP || 3 on CPU) is 24.6-28.7 ms of ViNT critical path against 23.2 ms for leaving the batch intact and splitting obs-vs-goal instead. Batch-1 also does NOT unlock HTA: removing the 6-frame Split removes the 'unsupported op StridedSlice' rejection, but the tile then fails on 'unsupported op Transpose' from EfficientNet's static-padding lowering, so ViNT still composes on no accelerator but the DSP.
_notes.gpu_fp16_lane: GPU fp16 measured on ViNT's tiles: decoder 16.4 ms, encoders 55.9 ms (DSP does the encoders in 14.2, so only the decoder is a candidate). Context init is 42 ms for the decoder and 256 ms for the encoders — a one-time bringup cost, not a per-dispatch one. Concurrency measured, not assumed: GPU+DSP 1.85x of an ideal 1.94x, GPU+HTA 1.14x of an ideal 1.16x.
_notes.vint_par_decoder_cpu_is_the_in_situ_valu: 28468 us, not the 14423 us measured in isolation. The slicing study's own trace of this exact tile on the CPU lane recorded 28.468 ms — 2.05x its isolated cell — while the GPU ran the same tile at 0.96x of its 16.4 ms cell in my run. Solved against the isolated number, MOSEK picks CPU (14.4 < 16.4) and then pays 28.5; solved against the in-situ number it picks the GPU and the prediction holds. This is the contention gap choosing a worse placement, not merely mispredicting one, which is the strongest argument yet for a contention term in the cost model.
_notes.tile_boundaries_determine_backend_eligib: Three independent instances now: FusedSensorNet's tail fails HTA on the boundary requantisation (Convert) when cut at the FC outputs but not at the conv outputs; yolov8n reaches HTA only when sliced from the nosplit rewrite; ViNT's decoder composes on GPU when cut at the compress Gemms and fails on L2Norm when cut one boundary earlier. Where a tile is cut decides which backends can run it, so slicing and placement cannot be optimised independently.
_notes.cells_rebuilt_from_in_situ: Cells for accelerator and single-threaded tiles are the MEDIAN of the per-placement in-situ p50 recorded by sweep qrb5165_20260829-200620 (12 points) and its periodic-only addendum (6 points), pooled over up to 41 placements per cell and requiring at least 5. Standalone cells are kept in _previous_cells_standalone. Rationale: standalone loop-mean cells ran 1.655x optimistic for tiles under 1 ms. A calibrated idle-gap measurement (measurements/calibration_gap_sweep.json) halves that error but leaves ~19% residual; the hypothesis that cost tracks the schedule's idle gap was tested against the traces and rejected (31% error, worse than any flat choice). Multi-threaded CPU tiles whose cost depends on what runs beside them are deliberately excluded -- see feedback_does_not_converge_for_contended_cpu_tiles.
_notes.residual_makespan_gap_is_scheduling_not_: After rebuilding cells from in-situ medians, per-tile accuracy went from 5/18 cells within +/-15% to 11/14, median per-tile ratio 1.147 -> 1.043. The MAKESPAN ratio only fell 1.230 -> 1.110. Since the parts are now predicted well and the whole is not, the remaining ~10% is scheduling -- gate waits, dependency stalls and lane queueing that make a schedule take longer than the sum of its correctly-predicted tiles. Chasing it with more cell measurement will not work; it needs a scheduling-side term.
_notes.in_situ_promotion_converges: Promoting in-situ medians was checked for convergence rather than assumed. Iteration 1 moved cells by +914%/+287%/+72%/-39%; iteration 2, pooling the runs produced by iteration 1's own schedules, moved 13 of 15 cells by <=4% (several by 0%). The exception is fused_tail@cpu at +18%, a multi-threaded CPU tile -- the same class as the cells excluded by feedback_does_not_converge_for_contended_cpu_tiles, and worth watching. Measured cost of the change: prediction error halved (median |ratio-1| 23.0% -> 11.0% over 3 A/B points, same tasksets and board conditions), but the schedules chosen got slightly SLOWER on 2 of 3 (+7.2%, +5.6%; -0.6% on the third). A more accurate model is not automatically a faster schedule.

conditions.cpu_affinity: UNMASKED. Superseded 2026-08-30: the block previously claimed 'taskset -c 4-5 for cpu cells (the lane's exec mask)', which contradicted this file's own cpu_cells_must_be_unmasked note and was wrong. The exec mask binds only the lane thread; the QNN CPU op package builds its thread pool at bringup with full-machine affinity, so a masked measurement does not describe how the runtime executes the tile. Cells sourced from in-situ medians carry the runtime's real affinity by construction.
conditions.why: Cells must be measured in the state the run executes in. Under schedutil the board idles at 710 MHz of 2419 and the accelerator cells come out 10-36% pessimistic — the host clock gates FastRPC dispatch, so DSP and HTA work is measured slow when the CPU is slow (yolov8n backbone on HTA: 21.6 ms under schedutil, 13.9 ms under performance). The previous cells are kept in _previous_cells_schedutil for comparison.
conditions.sweep_variance: Three independent 20-iteration sweeps under the same governor, same board, minutes apart: dronet@hta 1.96/2.01/1.61, yolov8n_backbone@dsp 13.10/12.83/12.24, yolov8n_head@dsp 15.82/15.94/16.08, mlp_control@cpu 0.10/0.09/0.03 ms. So a cell carries roughly +-10% of sweep-to-sweep spread (much more for sub-100us graphs, where the measurement is noise-dominated), which is the floor on prediction accuracy unless cells are taken as a median of repeated sweeps. The one systematic residual is yolov8n's head: every sweep puts it at 15.4-16.5 ms while in-situ it is consistently 17.2-17.3 ms, and single-shot measurement (N=1) gives 17.2 — the runtime dispatches each tile once per instance, not in a loop, so for this graph the loop mean is the wrong statistic.
conditions.statistic: Cells with a sufficient in-situ sample are the pooled median of per-placement in-situ p50 from sweep qrb5165_20260829-200620 (see cells_rebuilt_from_in_situ). Remaining cells keep their standalone measurement; _previous_cells_standalone holds the pre-rebuild values.

flowc_vint_nav_qrb5165_nav.note: in-situ medians from this run, promoted because a standalone cell cannot see lane contention

gpu_oppkg_cells._comment: GPU (Adreno 650) int8 cells, measured 2026-08-30 with the custom OpenCL op package in qnn_models/gpu_oppkg (libQnnGpuOpPackageFlowC.so). Kept in a separate block rather than merged into `cells` on purpose: these cells are only reachable when the runtime registers that op package via QnnBackend_registerOpPackage, which flowc/emit_runtime.py does not yet do, and they were taken under different conditions than the `cells` block (see gpu_oppkg_conditions). Merging them into `cells` would let the scheduler place int8 work on a GPU lane the emitted runtime cannot actually feed.
gpu_oppkg_cells.harness: qnn_models/gpu_oppkg/runtime/opbench.cpp -- same wallclock-around-QnnGraph_execute measurement as runtime/profile_segments.cpp, but composing from a converter-generated model library instead of a context binary (a context binary cannot carry op-package ops).
gpu_oppkg_cells.statistic: median of 200/100/50 iters, two independent repetitions reported as a/b

bringup_us._comment: compose+finalize, excluded from the cells above; the GPU pays a large one-off OpenCL program build.

accuracy._comment: int8 agreement, measured against the CPU/DSP backends on identical input bytes; full tables in qnn_models/gpu_oppkg/README.md.
accuracy.fused_vision_conv@gpu_vs_cpu: 95.3% exact, max 1 LSB (DSP vs CPU on the same tensors: 90.2%, max 2 LSB)
accuracy.dronet@gpu_vs_cpu: per-tensor exact rate >= the DSP's at every one of dronet's 21 intermediates; final steer differs by 6 LSB (DSP: 11)

gpu_oppkg_conditions.governor: schedutil (the brief for this work forbids changing the governor, so these cells are NOT directly comparable to the `cells` block, which was taken under `performance`)
gpu_oppkg_conditions.path: converter model library composed at run time, not a context binary
